# Only run installs on Colab or in the browser
import sys
import importlib.util

if 'google.colab' in str(get_ipython()):
    if importlib.util.find_spec("modelclass") is None:
        !apt-get -qq install -y graphviz
        !pip -qq install ModelFlowIb > /dev/null 2>&1
        !mkdir -p data && curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worldbank/MFMod-ModelFlow/main/models/Pakistan/data/pak_new.pcim -o data/pak_new.pcim

elif sys.platform == 'emscripten':  # in the browser: the book's live code (thebe-lite) or JupyterLite
    import micropip
    try:
        await micropip.install('modelflowib')
    except ValueError:
        # the older Pyodide of the book's live code has no pyarrow; modelflow only needs it
        # to save large models, so stand in a pyarrow that imports as "not installed"
        micropip.add_mock_package('pyarrow', '0', modules={'pyarrow': 'raise ImportError("no pyarrow in this browser")'})
        await micropip.install('modelflowib')
    # the browser has no data folder, so fetch the model file into one
    from pathlib import Path
    from pyodide.http import pyfetch
    if not Path('data/pak.pcim').exists():
        Path('data').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        response = await pyfetch('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IbHansen/modelflow-manual/main/model_repo/pak.pcim')
        Path('data/pak.pcim').write_bytes(await response.bytes())

To run a simulation, the following steps must invariably be followed.

Create a new DataFrame, typically a copy of an existing one.

Change the value in the new df of the variable(s) to be shocked.

Solve the model using the newly altered df as the input df.

records.content:
A simulation follows three steps:

Create a scenario DataFrame from a baseline using .upd(), which applies an update expression that sets, scales, or grows selected variables over a chosen time range.

Solve the model by calling it with the scenario DataFrame, a start and end year, and a keep= label that names the scenario for later comparison.

Inspect results on the returned DataFrame or directly on the model, which stores each kept scenario.

records.content:
Using the .upd() expression syntax<start end>  VAR1 VAR2 ...  <op>  value

Time range <start end> is optional; omit it to cover the full index.

Variables are space-separated; wildcards (*, ?) are supported.

Operators: = (set), + (add), * (multiply), % (percent change),
=growth / +growth (growth rate), =diff (difference).

Stacking more lines in the update string lets you shock several variables or time
ranges in one call.

To make tables and plots easier to read, we attach short descriptions to each emission variable and merge them into mpak.var_description. These labels can then be used instead of the raw codes wherever the model displays results.

var_descriptions = {
    'PAKCCEMISCO2CKN': 'Coal emissions, tCO2e',
    'PAKCCEMISCO2GKN': 'Natural Gas emissions, tCO2e',
    'PAKCCEMISCO2OKN': 'Crude Oil emissions, tCO2e',
    'PAKCCEMISCO2TKN': 'Total emissions, tCO2e',
}

mpak.var_description = mpak.var_description | var_descriptions

Recording sequence for the Venice talk (each step triggers a ~1 s graph morph):

Start on GDP PAKNYGDPMKTPCN, Up = 1, Down = 0 → small graph.

Increase Up: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 (pause ~2 s each) — GDP’s upstream drivers unfold.

Dropdown → PAKCCEMISCO2TKN (total emissions) — graph morphs to the emissions block.

Show the Chart and Attribution tabs — the $30-tax impact numbers.

Toggle Node display: Name → +values → +Attribution; flip orientation V → H.

Record the browser tab (OBS / Win+Alt+R) → export MP4 (H.264/AAC) → embed in PowerPoint.

Breakdown

Element

What it does

mpak

The model object holding the baseline and the latest simulation

['PAKCCEMISCO2*']

Select all variables matching the pattern — here, CO₂ emissions

.difpctlevel

Percent difference between the latest simulation and the baseline

.rename()

Use the variable descriptions

.df

Return the underlying pandas DataFrame (rows = years, columns = variables)

.T

Transpose so variables become rows and years become columns

.style.format("{:.2f}")

Render as a styled table with values shown to two decimal places

records.content:
Open the chapter 

Carbon tax in Pakistan.

Press the power button at the top of the page. It starts Python in the browser.

Run the cells from the top, in order. The first cells install ModelFlow into the
browser and download the Pakistan model. That takes a little while, and has to be done
again after the page is reloaded.

Edit any code cell and run it again, for example a different carbon tax.

Until a cell is run, the page shows the output stored when the book was built.
